- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.68 → 81.88 or 82.31), then corrects with a downward bias later.
- Underestimates in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when true prices rise more than forecasted.
- Shows mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained upward trends.
- Lagged response to recent price spikes: model reacts too slowly to recent highs, underestimating continuation or reversal.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum: forecasts often assume trend continuation without accounting for volatility or policy shocks.
- Avoids sharp downward corrections after spikes; tends to underestimate downside risk in volatile periods.
